hints.content:
We are trying to find a **unit rate**, specifically the number of strokes per $1$ hole.

$\dfrac{\blueE{\text{strokes}}}{\maroonD{\text{holes}}} = \purpleD{\text{strokes per hole}}$

We can compare from the largest to the smallest place value.

###Finding the unit rates

We divide based on the unit rate we want.

Golfer| $\blueE{\text{Total strokes}} $ ||  $\maroonD{\text{Holes played}}$||$\purpleD{\text{Strokes per hole}}$
- | :-: | :-:| :-:|:-:|:-:
Shanika |$43$|$\div$ | $9$|$\approx$|$4.8$
Alicia|$79$ |$\div$ |$18$ | $\approx$|$4.4$
Rickie|$123$ |$\div$ | $27$|$\approx$| $4.6 $

###Comparing the unit rates

Golfer| Ones | $.$ | Tenths
- | :-: | :-:| :-:|:-:|:-:
Shanika | $4$ | $.$ | $8$
Alicia| $4$ | $.$ | $\redE{4}$
Rickie| $4$ | $.$ | $6$

The golfers all have $4$ ones of strokes per hole, but Alicia has the least tenths of strokes per hole.

###Conclusion

Alicia had the lowest number of strokes per hole.

question.content:
Three different golfers played a different number of holes today.
Shanika played $9$ holes and had a total of $43$ strokes. Alicia played $18$ holes and had a total of $79$ strokes.  Rickie played $27$ holes and had a total of $123$ strokes.

**Which golfer had the lowest *number of strokes per hole*?**

[[☃ radio 1]]
